causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Hot temperatures and high humidity drove high demand, greater than forecast.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Constraints on the interconnectors between NSW and Queensland limited access to cheaper generation from NSW.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding by participants contributed to the high price. Rebids by Alinta Energy at Braemar and by Genuity at Millmerran power stations, meant that some high-priced capacity was needed for 2 intervals, setting the price at $15,500/MWh.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Around 1,470 MW was unavailable due to ongoing generator outages at Gladstone, Callide B and 2 units at Callide C.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Around 100 MW of low-priced capacity was unavailable due to technical issues at various coal power stations which arose late that afternoon, in part due to the high temperatures.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: This reduced limit was due to a network outage around Lismore in NSW.

interconnectors_named.name: Queensland-NSW Interconnector (QNI)
interconnectors_named.quote: During the 2 high-priced intervals, flows on Queensland-NSW Interconnector (QNI) were limited to around 500 MW, 200 MW less than its current nominal limit.

interconnectors_named.name: Terranora interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: The same outage forced flows of around 80 MW on the Terranora interconnector from Queensland to NSW, even though price was higher in Queensland.

intervals.quote: Between 6.30 pm and 7 pm that evening, the average 30-minute price reached $5,674/MWh.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Network limitations, which impacted the interconnectors, meant that South Australia had limited access to cheaper generation from Victoria: − At times the flows on Murraylink into South Australia were around 20% of its nominal limit. − Flows on Heywood were, at times, 50 MW lower than it's limit of 600 MW.
